# Changelog

All notable changes to Document Graph Explorer are documented here.

This project follows the Keep a Changelog format.

## [Unreleased]

### Breaking
- **New Resonance workspace.** The floating toolbar workspace is replaced by a dark three-column layout (Graph / Library / Export tabs, a filter sidebar and a "Why they're connected" inspector). The View/Analyze/Data toolbar, floating filter bar and graph navigator are gone, and a fresh profile now opens in 2D. The README was rewritten to match ([#137](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/137), [#143](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/143), [#173](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/173), [#247](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/247)).
- **Some sound tags were merged or renamed.** noise, vocal breath and synth stab were merged ([#197](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/197)); seven look-alike DJ tags now use their common names ([#224](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/224)); turntable shows as vinyl scratch ([#213](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/213)), vocal harmony as choir ([#214](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/214)), acid bass as acid synth ([#215](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/215)), foley hit as foley ([#225](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/225)), and downlifter as falling ([#205](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/205)). Saved filters or tag corrections that use the old names may no longer match.
- **Fewer tags in the tag picker.** Rarely used tags are hidden until you search for them ([#218](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/218), [#229](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/229); eleven came back in [#223](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/223)), and the distorted and reverse effect tags are hidden until they pass testing on real clips ([#200](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/200)).
- **Saved audio analyses are recomputed.** Tagger updates bump the audio analysis revision (for example [#251](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/251), [#262](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/262), [#267](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/267)), so previously saved analyses refresh the next time the library loads.
- **AI settings migration.** The AI plumbing refactor migrates saved AI settings to the new shape ([#24](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/24)).

### Added
- **For you** is the home when a library is only sounds. It keeps a player and the clip's tags in front, shelves what sounds alike by the stored fingerprint, and leaves the graph one tab away as **Sound map**. A document or a mix of sounds and documents still opens on the graph.
- **Find similar sounds** ranks the stored CLAP fingerprint. Shared labels, tempo and key stay as the explanation. Clips that only share a tag no longer outrank a recording that actually sounds alike.
- **Load audio demo** on the welcome screen. It builds eight short clips in the browser (kick, snare, hat, shaker, two bass loops, a pad and a pluck) and ingests them on this device, so the sound graph can be tried without a sample pack.
- Gemini 3.7 Flash (`google/gemini-3.7-flash`) in the OpenRouter chat and enrichment model pickers. Chat lists it with the other fast-tier options; enrichment lists it next to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite so corpus runs can use the latest Flash without leaving the cheap tier. ([#75](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/75))
- Additional curated OpenRouter models that fill provider gaps: enrichment adds GPT-5.6 Luna, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and MiniMax M3; chat adds GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Luna. Defaults stay Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite (enrichment).
- **Add a folder** (Google Drive-style folder ingest): a first-class picker on the welcome screen and toolbar that selects a directory once and ingests every relevant file inside it, subfolders included — no drilling into subfolders or drag-and-drop required. Uses `window.showDirectoryPicker()` where available, falling back to a `webkitdirectory` folder-upload picker elsewhere; both paths run the same relevance filters as a folder drop (`.gitignore`, ignored dirs, lockfiles, dotfiles, size caps, ignored-tray routing). One-shot import — live syncing stays with the corpus switcher's "Watch a folder". ([#16](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/16))
- Source-code and repository ingest: dropping a project folder (or picking `.ts`/`.py`/`.go`/`.rs` and similar files) parses them as graph documents. Relative imports, includes, and `mod` declarations become high-confidence reference edges, resolved against the importing file's path (including extensionless specifiers and `index.ts` / `__init__.py`). Folder walks honor `.gitignore`, skip lockfiles and minified bundles, and ignore additional build trees (`vendor`, `target`, `coverage`, …). ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Visual snapshot compare: **Compare** in the snapshots drawer paints added (green) and updated (amber) documents on the live graph, lists titles that exist only in the snapshot, and frames the changed set. ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Graph filter facets for connection kind (links / similar / keywords / entities) and recency (any time / 30d / 90d / 1y). Search results and scene emphasis intersect the active filter (search ∩ filter). ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Settings **About** shows this origin's IndexedDB usage vs quota, with a warning toast when ingest starts and storage is ≥90% full. ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Selective cache eviction: uncheck **Cache embeddings for instant reload**, or **Clear embeddings** / **Clear original files**, without wiping the graph. ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Recognition settings: scanned-PDF OCR language (English bundled; extra Tesseract packs drop into `public/ocr/lang/`) and page cap (10/20/40/80). Semantic search can skip BGE's English instruction prefix for mixed-language queries. ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Installable web app: `manifest.webmanifest` plus theme-color / apple-touch metadata (no service worker — keeps the air-gap CSP). Linux AppImage target via `npm run dist:linux`. ([#15](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/15))
- Security headers on all deployment targets: `Permissions-Policy` (camera/microphone/geolocation/payment/usb/serial disabled) and `Strict-Transport-Security` (`max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`) in `vercel.json`, Docker nginx headers, and the `DEPLOYMENT.md` nginx example. Vite dev headers get `Permissions-Policy` only (no HSTS on plain HTTP). ([#12](https://github.com/chrisatom1998/document-graph-explorer/pull/12))
- usd-agent (`tools/usd_pipeline/usd_agent.py`): an LLM agent whose tools are OpenUSD stage operations — ask natural-language questions about an exported corpus stage (clusters, documents, connections with evidence, view variants) and it answers by querying prims via `usd-core`, never by guessing. Providers: OpenRouter (cloud), Ollama (local), or a network-free mock used by its `selftest` mode, which exercises every tool plus the full agent loop against a real stage.
- Performance benchmarks (`docs/benchmarks.md`): measured ingest throughput (~11 docs/s end-to-end on the 100-PDF demo corpus), layout convergence from 100 to 2,000 nodes (under 6 s to settle at 2,000 via the production worker driven headless by `npm run bench:layout`), render frame rate (holds the 120 Hz frame cap through 2,000 nodes / 8,400 edges), and OpenUSD export build time (linear, 19 ms at 2,000 nodes), with methodology and caveats.
- OpenUSD export: **Data → Export OpenUSD scene** serializes the graph as a composed `.usda` stage — document/topic nodes as Sphere prims carrying a `docGraph:` custom-attribute schema (title, topics, entities, keywords, status), edges as one BasisCurves prim per kind with parallel weight/evidence arrays, translucent cluster hulls, and a `graphView` variantSet switching detailed vs summary views. Validated against stock `usdchecker`. A new Python pipeline CLI (`tools/usd_pipeline/usd_pipeline.py`, Pixar `usd-core`) re-validates every schema invariant, exercises the variants through composition, and packages `.usdz`; see `docs/openusd-pipeline.md`.
